author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected through the existing visit form, reached by its address alone. The correction follows the booking rules, changes that visit in place, and returns to the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the existing visit form with its `visit` attribute prefilled with that visit's current date and description.

Given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are posted to the same URL, then that visit carries them, the pet has the same number of visits, and the response redirects to the owner detail page.
Given a blank description, when the correction is posted, then it is refused with the description named, the form is redisplayed, and the stored visit is unchanged.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is posted, then it is refused with the date named, the form is redisplayed, and the stored visit is unchanged.
Edge case 3: opening or correcting a visit is refused when the pet does not belong to the named owner, the visit does not belong to the named pet, or the visit does not exist; no visit changes.
Edge case 4: a visit already dated today or earlier opens prefilled with its current date, and resubmitting that date is refused.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit (NG-5) or deleting one (NG-4).
Any edit link on the owner detail page: the form is reachable by its URL alone in this request.
Changing any visit field other than its date and description, or moving a visit to another pet.
A confirmation message after a correction, or new submit wording on the form: neither is in the request, and new wording must exist in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002).
notes: Owner statements: intake line 1. Reuse the template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its `visit` model attribute, as the request states. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md under the narrowest reading: visible entry point (deferred by the owner); correcting a visit dated today or earlier without moving its date; dedicated wording for the correction form and outcome. The form therefore keeps its 'Add Visit' button. REQ-VIS-002's list of earlier visits is not extended to corrections; what the reused form shows there is a design choice. For the owner of docs/adr/README.md: the index needs a row for docs/adr/2026-10-30-non-goal-visit-correction.md, which is outside this agent's write scope. The prior non-goal ADR carries an Amended line; its Accepted status stands because NG-4 is unchanged.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the owner feature unchanged in shape: no new module, type, or pattern. Correction reaches the visit through the Owner aggregate root (system-design § Contracts invariants) and saves through OwnerRepository, mirroring the pet edit flow in PetController. Adjustments: VisitController's `visit` model attribute branches on an optional visitId, the way PetController.findPet branches on an optional petId; Pet gains an identity lookup and Owner a correction entry point beside addVisit; Visit binding narrows to an allow-list. Basis is a read of the sources and grep; the IDE oracle is not connected. The non-future date check stays the one recorded controller deviation: both handlers share one private method, so the deviation is not widened (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog). No ADR: nothing here constrains later slices beyond the existing briefs.
integration_points: Binding, GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit: `visit` is a persisted type behind an allow-list. Add @InitBinder("visit") allowing date and description only; the existing id disallow list stays. The non-goal on other visit fields rests on this list.

Binding, POST edit handler: take the owner with @ModelAttribute(binding = false), or resolve it without a bound parameter. Owner is a persisted type and must not bind here. The handler also binds no other request-derived object.

Model attribute: on the edit route loadPetWithVisit returns a copy of the stored visit carrying its id, date, and description, and does NOT add it to pet.visits. The booking route's new Visit plus pet.addVisit stays as is. The copy's id keeps visit['new'] false, so the unchanged template shows no 'New' heading.

Write path: new Owner method beside addVisit taking pet id, visit id, date, and description; it finds the stored visit through Pet's new lookup and sets the two fields, then the handler calls owners.save(owner). No flash message on success (prd-entry non-goals); redirect to redirect:/owners/{ownerId}.

Refusal: unknown owner, pet, or visit, and a visit outside the named pet, throw IllegalArgumentException from the @ModelAttribute method, as the owner and pet cases do today. It runs on GET and POST, so no write is reached. The message carries identifiers only (security-principles § Language Realization, secret disclosure row).

Template: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is unchanged. The form posts to its own URL. On the edit route Previous Visits lists every stored visit, the one under correction included, always at stored values; that is the design answer to the prd-entry's open point. Button stays 'Add Visit'.

Double, repository boundary in VisitControllerTests: the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository, a framework stub kept because the class fixture already stubs it and a hand double must implement all of a Spring Data interface. Assert unchanged state on the fixture's stored Visit and verify no save on refusal.

Double, repository boundary for in-place update: a real H2 store through ClinicServiceTests' existing data-JPA setup, no double. One test loads the owner, applies the correction, saves, reloads, and asserts the same visit id, new values, and same visit count. A stub cannot show that the merge inserts no row.
Double, domain units: real Owner, Pet, and Visit objects in OwnerTests for the lookup and correction entry point. Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness.

patterns.description: findPet: model attribute branching on an optional path variable
updatePetDetails: apply accepted fields to the stored child through the owner, then save the owner
getPet(Integer): identity lookup to mirror on Pet
addVisit: aggregate-root entry point to sit beside

risks.risk: Phantom visit: loadPetWithVisit runs before every handler and adds a new Visit to the pet, so reusing it on the edit route cascades an extra row on save, breaching the 'same number of visits' bullet of REQ-VIS-003.
risks.mitigation: Branch on visitId as above; the copy is never added to pet.visits. The real-store test proves it (system-design § Contracts invariants).

risks.risk: Rejected input leaks into stored state or the Previous Visits table when the form binds directly to the stored visit; mock fixtures would also hide or fake 'stored visit unchanged'.
risks.mitigation: Bind to the copy; apply to the stored visit only after validation passes (architecture-principles Design Principle 7, fail secure; system-design § Contracts invariants).

risks.risk: Mass assignment through the Owner parameter: the booking route binds the loaded Owner from request parameters and saves it. Copying that signature lets a correction POST change owner fields.
risks.mitigation: No Owner binding on the edit route, and the Visit allow-list (security-principles § Language Realization, mass assignment row; system-design § Threat Model). The booking route is out of scope and is recorded in the Threat Model row. A test posts an owner field to the edit route and asserts the owner is unchanged.

risks.risk: Blank date on correction: the booking check skips a null date and the schema allows null, so copying it would erase a booked visit's date.
risks.mitigation: The correction refuses a blank date with field error typeMismatch.visitDate: a blank is not a date later than today, so this is the recorded rule, not a new one. The shared private method keeps the booking route's null skip at its call site, leaving that route's behavior unchanged. Add one test beyond the prd-entry names. Booking's gap is recorded in system-design § Known Defects (security-principles § Trust Boundaries, external input row).

risks.risk: Widening the controller-rule deviation by a second copy of the date check.
risks.mitigation: One private method called from both handlers; no new rule in the controller (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row and the paragraph after the table).

risks.risk: The date input's min attribute blocks browser resubmission of a past-dated visit, so a browser check could look like the refusal of edge case 4.
risks.mitigation: The server check is the refusal; the test posts through MockMvc, which ignores min. minVisitDate stays unchanged (security-principles § Trust Boundaries, external input row).

risks.risk: Path: searching one pet's visits by identity (system-design § Scale and Load, 'One pet's visits' row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: a linear scan of the eagerly loaded visits.

notes: Durable writes: REQ-VIS-003 joined the Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController Contracts rows; added § Scale and Load, absent from this older brief, with its first row; added the correction invariant; extended Security Context inputs and the mass-assignment Threat Model row; added a derived, unconfirmed Known Defects row for blank-date booking and generalized that section's lead sentence; added the ADR index row for 2026-10-30-non-goal-visit-correction.md as the prd-entry asked. The booking findings (Owner binding, blank date) come from reading the code and were not exercised. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records. Effort is involved for the model-attribute and binding subtleties, despite the small surface.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: LOW, not exercised at runtime in this review: the correction route inherits the booking route's unbounded visit description. Visit.java carries only @NotBlank on description (`grep -rn -F -e '@Size' src/main` hits only model/Person.java:32 and :37), while db/h2/schema.sql:62 reads `description VARCHAR(255)` and db/mysql/schema.sql:54 reads `description VARCHAR(255),`, so a POST of 256 or more characters should end in a generic 500 at save instead of a refused form on those two vendors. Reach is no wider than POST /visits/new already gives: the save fails with no stored change, and an unauthenticated caller gains nothing over the recorded baseline. A length rule on Visit would also change the booking route, which the slice's bullets do not name, and it adds a rule beyond 'the same rules as a booking', so any fix is a product decision for a later slice.
approved_aspects: Mass assignment on Visit, cleared by resolving the binders in VisitController.java:53-61: line 55 `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");` applies to every binder and line 60 `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");` narrows `visit`. Visit declares no other bindable field or association (Visit.java read), and the write uses the path's visitId, never the bound copy's id (VisitController.java:158 `owner.correctVisit(petId, visitId, visit.getDate(), visit.getDescription());`), so a forged id could not redirect the write even past the binder.

Mass assignment on Owner: the edit handler declares `@ModelAttribute(binding = false) Owner owner` (VisitController.java:150), so the persisted aggregate saved at line 159 takes no request parameters; VisitControllerTests' theVisitEditSubmissionShouldLeaveTheOwnerUnchangedWhenAnOwnerFieldIsPosted pins it. The booking route's bound Owner at line 126 is unchanged by this diff and already recorded in the system-design Threat Model row, so it is baseline, not a finding.

Object-level scoping and cross-request state: loadPetWithVisit re-resolves owner, pet, and visit from the path on every GET and POST (VisitController.java:73-87), and Pet.findVisit searches only that pet's visits, so a pet outside the owner or a visit outside the pet throws before any handler runs. Owner.correctVisit re-checks both inside the aggregate. Parameterized tests cover the three refused addresses on both verbs and assert no save.

Validation at the boundary: the edit POST carries `@Valid Visit visit` (line 151) and rejectUnlessInTheFuture refuses null, today, and earlier dates server-side (lines 163-166), so the browser's min attribute is not the control. The booking route's null-date skip is preserved at its call site (line 128), so the extraction weakens no check; `@InitBinder("visit")` tightens that route rather than loosening it.

Fail secure on refusal: the form binds to a detached copy built in copyOfStoredVisit, never the stored visit, and application.properties:11 reads `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false`, so a refused correction cannot flush. The stored visit changes only in correctVisit after hasErrors is false.

Output and injection: description and date redisplay through th:field and th:text; `grep -rn -F -e 'th:utext' -e '[(${' src/main/resources/templates` returned nothing. The template's `__${name}__` preprocessing in fragments/inputField.html takes only the literal 'date' and 'description' from createOrUpdateVisitForm.html:32-33, no request text. The redirect target is expanded from the int-typed ownerId path variable, and no query text is built in this diff.

Errors: the new exception messages carry integer identifiers only (`"Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + pet.getId() + "."`, VisitController.java:103, and `"Invalid Visit identifier!"` in Owner.correctVisit), so nothing sensitive can reach error.html's `${message}` line.

Exposed surface: the two new routes show and change a visit's date and description, data the owner page already displays, to any caller, inside the recorded unauthenticated baseline (system-design Threat Model row 'Unauthenticated data modification' names visit creation and edit routes). No actuator or management setting changed: `python3 scripts/changeset.py --name-only` lists no properties file.

Secrets and dangerous sinks: a case-insensitive sweep of the changeset's added lines for password, secret, token, api key, credential, Runtime, ProcessBuilder, exec(, JsonTypeInfo, Files., /tmp/, System.out/err, logger, createQuery, nativeQuery, and utext hit only the docs line on datasource credentials, an existing sentence re-emitted by the diff with no value in it.

Supply chain: no dependency change (`git status --short build.gradle gradle pom.xml` printed nothing and the changeset lists none). No NVD match ran, the recorded standing gap; `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath --offline` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.2, spring-webmvc 7.0.10, jackson-databind 3.1.7, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, hibernate-core 7.4.13.Final. The IntelliJ oracle was not connected, so the binder and route claims rest on grep and file reads, the weaker basis. ./gradlew test was not re-run here; the review relies on the build-pass at line 7, and the tests were read, not executed.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit's date and description

blast_radius.note: All code sits in the owner package, but the change has 56 hunks across 12 files, adds an unauthenticated write route on a flagged security surface, makes booked visits mutable for the first time, and alters the loadPetWithVisit and binder code that also runs on the booking route.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks show no code-level defect: booking keeps its null-date skip and its allow-list has no practical effect, and the copy stays out of pet.visits. The surprise is what the rules produce: every seeded visit is dated 2013, so fixing a past visit's typo means moving its date into the future. The PRD records this as an open question. A POST that omits a field, rather than blanking it, also silently keeps the stored value.

test_adequacy.note: The controller tests are real: they cover today, yesterday, blank date, cross-pet addresses, no save on refusal, and no added visit. The gap is persistence: the design block says the store test proves the merge adds no row, but that test is @Transactional, so it saves a managed entity, while production merges a detached graph with open-in-view off. Prefill is asserted on the model only, never in rendered HTML.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved and late-round approvals carry no recommendations, and the citations spot-checked resolve. The security approval carries a caveat: a description over 255 characters should produce a 500 on H2 and MySQL rather than a refused form. It was not exercised at runtime, it is deferred to a later slice, and neither the PRD nor system-design records it. Security did not re-review the fix round, which is sound because that delta touched only tests and docs.

scope_deviation.note: No retries, consultations, or design revisions. The diff matches the request: no owner-page link, no cancelling, and only date and description change.
